newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. oil experts end Iraq mission.
newsitem.headline: U.N. oil experts end Iraq mission.

text.p: Three United Nations oil experts left Iraq on Sunday after inspecting the country's oil facilities for possible implementation of a delayed oil-for-food deal with the the world body, a U.N. source in Baghdad said.
The source said the three specialists hired from the Dutch- based Saybolt firm ended a week's mission in Iraq visiting the southern Mina al-Bakr oil terminal and the Iraqi-Turkish oil pipeline.
They checked Iraq's metering equipment and oil facilities to see whether they can handle exports under the oil deal with U.N., he said.

The deal allows Iraq partial oil sales worth $2 billion in six months to raise money for food and medical supplies to alleviate the effects of U.N. sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Baghdad intends to export 450,000 barrels per day (bpd) via Turkey out of its limited oil exports estimated at 700,000 and 800,000 bpd at current prices. The remainder is planned to be pumped through terminals in the Gulf.

The deal, signed in May, was stalled because of security concerns in northern Iraq sparked by Baghdad's dispatch of troops in August to help a Kurdish faction fighting a rival. The fighting, meanwhile, halted under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
